items.text: The need to sleep interferes with other more biologically pressing needs, such as finding and gathering food, building shelter, and anything else you might do to ensure that your genetic line lives on. <break time="0.8s" /> Sleep is so important, yet so poorly understood, that it led one biologist to say, If sleep does not serve an absolutely vital function, it is the greatest mistake evolution ever made. <break time="0.8s" /> That function is still a mystery. <break time="0.8s" /> It would be nice to say that sleep is nothing more than the time when a body rests, but that would not be quite right either. <break time="0.8s" /> You can relax in a hammock on a beach all day long if you want to, but after about twenty hours you will be in pretty bad shape if you do not fall asleep and stay that way for a while. <break time="0.8s" /> Humans need roughly one hour of sleep for every two hours they are awake, and the body innately knows when this ratio becomes unbalanced. <break time="0.8s" /> Each hour of missed sleep one night will result in deeper sleep the next, until the bodys sleep debt is wiped clean.
